slides.headline: A SELF-EMPLOYED OWNER PASTED 3 MONTHS OF STATEMENTS INTO CLAUDE AND FOUND $8,400 HER CPA HAD MISSED FOR TWO YEARS.
slides.image_prompt: Dario Amodei in green accountant eyeshade, triumphant grin at camera, red pen in hand, bundled $100 bills visible, warm diner booth, tungsten light, documentary style, sharp focus on face, minimal background.

slides.headline: YOUR ACCOUNTANT READ THESE RECEIPTS. YOU PAID $300 AN HOUR. HE STILL MISSED FOUR.
slides.body: She had filed with the same CPA for six years and paid him to review the same records every time. One Claude session found what he missed, prompt by prompt, deduction by deduction.
slides.image_prompt: Overhead close shot: two hands mid-motion spreading printed bank statement pages across a dark navy desk, papers overlapping and half-crumpled, a receipt pile caught mid-scatter at the corner. Laptop screen at upper frame edge glowing with two columns of green checkmark and red X symbols — no text anywhere. No face, wrists and hands only. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, slight film grain. Accent: cool white paper against deep navy desk.

slides.headline: 1) SCAN YOUR BANK STATEMENTS IN 60 SECONDS
slides.body: She pasted three months of statements into Claude and got the same itemized breakdown a CPA bills $150 to $300 an hour to produce, in under a minute, free. Her car expenses were the single largest flagged category.

slides.headline: 2) PICK THE VEHICLE DEDUCTION THAT PAYS MORE
slides.body: The bank scan flagged her car as the biggest missed category. Most owners default to the IRS mileage rate without running the numbers, but the right choice is often worth $1,500 to $4,000 more in deductions per year.

slides.headline: $300/HR. CLAUDE CHARGES NOTHING.
slides.body: That is what accountants bill per hour to go through your records. You have already paid for every receipt in this post. You should not also pay someone to read them

slides.headline: 3) MAX YOUR RETIREMENT CONTRIBUTION THIS YEAR
slides.body: Vehicle math settled. Claude moved to retirement next. A Solo 401k lets a self-employed owner shelter up to $70,000 from taxes in a single year, most underfund it because the contribution math is confusing.

slides.headline: 4) CLAIM THE HOME OFFICE THE RIGHT WAY
slides.body: Retirement maxed, Claude ran the home office comparison. The simplified method caps the deduction at $1,500 per year. The actual expense method, based on real rent and utilities, often pays three to four times more.
slides.image_prompt: Three-quarter overhead: hands gripping a spiral notepad on a stainless-steel kitchen counter, the open page filled with checkmark symbols and dollar signs — no readable words. Hanging copper pots and a commercial range blurred warm in the burgundy-tinted background. Figure cut at the wrists, no face. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, slight film grain. Accent: cream notepad page against deep burgundy kitchen shadow.

slides.headline: 5 & 6) INDUSTRY WRITE-OFFS THEN CALCULATE WHAT YOU OWE
slides.body: Home office settled. General CPAs miss the write-offs specific to your industry, construction, food service, and creative fields add $2,000 to $8,000 most owners never claim. Missing a quarterly estimated payment triggers an IRS underpayment penalty at roughly 8% annualized.
slides.image_prompt: Close three-quarter shot: hands pressing a thick red marker ring around one date square on a wall calendar, red ink just bleeding at the edge, the bold circle unmistakably dominant. Below it on the table a laptop screen shows a single large red downward-arrow symbol — no text. Stark white calendar page, signal red ring. No face. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, slight film grain. Accent: signal red circle against stark white calendar page.
